summary: This paper establishes definitive topological, algebraic, and spectral boundaries for extending Huang-optimal signings to general d-regular graphs and Cartesian products. It proves a universal complex torus-holonomy no-go theorem ruling out S^2 = dI for non-bipartite Cartesian products over all of C, characterizes the complex-vs-real signing dichotomy on complete graphs Kq via conference and skew-Hadamard matrices, introduces non-bipartite Clifford-cube lifting, and provides an exhaustive zero-float switching-class atlas across 11 canonical regular graphs. All results are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 and zero-float Python.
